text.headline: A History of Machine Learning
text.text: Key moments in the development of algorithms, mathematics, statistics, and AI.

text.headline: Bayes' Theorem is Published
text.text: Thomas Bayes' work on conditional probability, published posthumously, underpins much of modern probabilistic machine learning.

text.headline: Principal Component Analysis is Introduced
text.text: Karl Pearson develops PCA, a foundational technique for reducing dimensionality in data.

text.headline: The Turing Test
text.text: Alan Turing publishes 'Computing Machinery and Intelligence,' proposing a test for machine intelligence.

text.headline: The Dartmouth Workshop
text.text: A summer workshop at Dartmouth College where the term 'Artificial Intelligence' is coined, marking the field's formal beginning.

text.headline: The Perceptron
text.text: Frank Rosenblatt develops the perceptron, an early neural network capable of learning.

media.caption: Mark I Perceptron, from the operator's manual

text.headline: Deep Blue Beats Garry Kasparov
text.text: IBM's Deep Blue becomes the first computer to beat a reigning world chess champion in a match.

text.headline: The Deep Learning Renaissance Begins
text.text: Geoffrey Hinton introduces deep belief networks, reviving interest in deep neural networks.

text.headline: IBM Watson Wins Jeopardy!
text.text: Watson defeats two of the show's greatest champions, demonstrating advanced natural language processing.

text.headline: AlphaGo Beats Lee Sedol
text.text: DeepMind's AlphaGo defeats a world champion Go player, a game long considered too complex for computers to master.

text.headline: ChatGPT Launches
text.text: OpenAI's ChatGPT brings large language models to mainstream public use, becoming one of the fastest-growing consumer applications in history.
